an issue was reported: "#0 The record id is not actually unique, so the new dedupe silently drops distinct captures that hash alike
src/energy.ts builds `id` as `md5(time + sessionID + prompt)` and src/energy.store.ts `dedupeRecords` treats it as identity — first occurrence wins, later lines with the same id are dropped at every rebuild and at the flush. But the key does not cover the rest of the record, so two *distinct* captures can share it: (1) same millisecond, same session and same prompt but different measurements (the compaction request's `extractUserPrompt` is the same last user message as the concurrent primary's, and two captures landing in the same millisecond is enough) — verified: records `{id:'same', energy:[1]}` and `{id:'same', energy:[2]}` written back to back leave **one** record in the view, permanently (every later rebuild re-dedupes from the durable state, which keeps both); (2) the concatenation has no separators, so boundaries collide too — verified `md5(t + 'ses_1' + '23') === md5(t + 'ses_12' + '3')`, two different session/prompt pairs sharing one id. Either way a real capture disappears from the repository view with no diagnostic — silent under-counting of energy, the mirror image of the double-count this key was added to prevent. Fix: make the hash cover the distinguishing parts of the record (e.g. the `energy` values and `url`, or the whole record minus the id), or append a per-capture nonce — copies stay identical because the id is computed once per capture and travels with the record to every mirror and merge, so the readers-dedupe contract is unaffected. Pin with a test that writes two same-time same-prompt captures with different energy and asserts both survive the rebuild and the flush. ". is it actually possible to have multiple energy records for a single prompt in a single session? do any specs allow for that?
